previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with a history of chronic pancreatitis, was admitted with a five-day history of epigastric abdominal pain radiating to the back, nausea, vomiting, and oliguria. She was managed with NPO status, IV hydration, and pain control using non-narcotic medications due to allergies. Her symptoms improved over the course of the admission, with resolution of leukocytosis and return of normal urine output. She gradually advanced to a regular diet and tolerated oral medications. No imaging or procedures were performed. She was discharged home in stable condition with no changes to her medication regimen and instructions to follow up with her primary care provider.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ with chronic pancreatitis here with symptoms consistent with

# Acute on chronic pancreatitis: Patient presented ___ three 
days of nausea, vomiting and abdominal pain similar to prior 
flares of acute pancreatitis. She was no longer able to tolerate 
her PO pain regimen or maintain adequate fluid intake so she was 
admitted to the hospital for symptom control. KUB showed stool 
in the colon but no signs of obstruction and triglycerides were 
in the 400s, improved from recent baseline. No clear inciting 
factor for this flare. Midline was placed and patient was 
treated with IVF, IV dilaudid, IV toradol, phenergan, and ativan 
as per protocol. As her ability to take adequate PO increased, 
her therapy was de-escalated until she was discharged back on 
her home regimen. She should continue to follow-up with her PCP 
for her pain management issues. 

CHRONIC ISSUES
# Anxiety/Depression - She was on IV ativan while NPO and then 
transitioned back to her home regimen once able to tolerate. She 
will continue to follow-up with her outpatient psychiatrist
# Migraines - None in the hospital. Continued Lamictal 200 mg po 
qam and 100 mg po qpm as tolerated

radiology_notes.text:
EXAM:  Abdomen supine and upright views.

CLINICAL INFORMATION:  Abdominal pain, history of pancreatitis, evaluate for
obstruction.

___.

FINDINGS:  Supine and upright views of the abdomen were obtained.  There is a
non-obstructive bowel gas pattern.  A moderate to abundant amount of stool is
seen throughout the colon.  No large air-fluid levels are seen.  There is no
evidence of free air.  Surgical clips are seen in the right upper quadrant
from presumed prior cholecystectomy.  Pelvic phleboliths are seen.

IMPRESSION:  No evidence of bowel obstruction or free air.  Moderate to
abundant amount of colonic fecal loading may be due to constipation.
